correctness.rationale: For all finite p>0, positive A,B,C,D and Haar T^2, two torus rotations remove three phases and leave cross phase arg(ad/(bc)). Integration in one circle gives Phi_s(X,Y), s=p/2. The recurrence for squared generalized binomial coefficients yields the exact identity Phi_XY = s^2/sqrt(XY) E[cos t (X+Y+2sqrt(XY)cos t)^(s-1)] for X,Y>0, X!=Y. Its strict sign is sign(p-2). Continuous extension through the diagonal supplies strict super/submodular four-corner inequalities without assuming finite pointwise second derivatives everywhere. Explicit overlap of the two cosine superlevel arcs decreases with phase distance from 0 to pi. Integration against mixed differences proves strictly decreasing (p>2) or increasing (p<2) moments and the exact extremizing cross phases. Orthogonality handles p=2; a zero amplitude makes one marginal constant. An exact integer convolution checker verifies M4(0)=36,M4(pi)=20,M6(0)=400,M6(pi)=112 for unit magnitudes; 944 supplementary numerical assertions passed. Numerical sampling is not used to establish universal quantifiers. A separate finite-difference test checked the nonstandard derivative identity at seven exponents.

originality.rationale: Full relevant sections of Gressman et al. arXiv:2106.12538 and Rains 1978 were compared by implications, not title alone. Gressman gives dependent-set failure for some exponent interval and the universal even-exponent theorem, but does not establish the complete phase ordering across every exponent for the single four-point rectangle; Rains is a global group-level result. The closest publicly available four-point-rectangle research classifies Fourier zero counts on finite cyclic grids under equal magnitudes, not Lp moments on the continuous torus. The closest four-point phase-only fourth-moment result works in a one-dimensional prime cyclic group and at one exponent. The new theorem computes the phase order uniformly in arbitrary positive magnitudes at all positive exponents, including the complete equality and boundary cases. A classical rearrangement formulation not indexed under these terms remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: Older rearrangement theory or older majorant literature may encode the exact rectangle phase monotonicity without the four-frequency terminology.
Bachelis 1973 full text and Bennett-Bez 2012 complete primary material were not fully inspected; accessible metadata does not indicate a decisive exact rectangle formula.
Searches and the stated single literature review do not certify priority relative to all published or unpublished work.

value.rationale: The rectangle is the first nontrivial affine dependence spanning a two-dimensional Fourier torus and is a standard natural benchmark for the Hardy-Littlewood majorant problem. The theorem supplies the complete all-exponent optimization of complex coefficient phases for every positive magnitude pattern, including a universal p=2 transition, strict ordering at intermediate phases and uniqueness of extrema. These structural facts go far beyond the routine p=2 orthogonality or p=4 convolution expansion, and exhibit an exceptional dependent support with fixed-modulus phase alignment throughout the entire p>2 range. They are potentially useful as exact model cases for phase alignment and support-sensitive majorants without relying on speculative downstream consequences.
